metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Russia strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Omar, have you thought about what we can get Adam for his celebration? I was thinking maybe a bottle of champagne would be nice. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: I think that's a good idea, but maybe something more personal would be better. My parents always taught me that a thoughtful gift is more important than an expensive one. What if we get him a framed photo of our class or something that reminds him of his time here?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: That's a sweet idea, but I still think the champagne is a good choice. It's a classic way to celebrate achievements. By the way, do you think one of the main goals in life is to make our parents proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: For me, it's definitely one of the most important goals. My parents have always sacrificed so much for me, and making them proud is the least I can do. In Russian culture, family is very important, and I think it's natural to want to make them proud. Champagne is okay, but I still think something more personal would mean more to Adam.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: I don't really see meaningful differences here, and at the end of the day it's all the same. People figure it out, and as long as we're speaking the same language, doesn't matter to me. Let's just live and let live, right? With experience, you can handle any situation. So, about that champagne for Adam...
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand what you're saying, but for me, making my parents proud is not just about handling situations, it's about respecting our traditions and values. It's a big part of who I am. And about the gift, I'm still not convinced champagne is the best choice, can't we think of something that shows we really care about Adam's achievement?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I'm not trying to convince you to change your values or anything, I just don't think making my parents proud is that big of a deal to me, personally. And okay, fine, let's brainstorm more ideas for Adam's gift, but I still think champagne is a nice gesture...
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I'm not trying to convince you either, I just know that for me, making my parents proud is a top priority. It's not just about them, it's about our family's honor and reputation. Let's think about something that really shows Adam we're happy for him, like a customized trophy or a heartfelt letter from our class.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: Honestly, I don't really care about making my parents proud, it's not something that drives me. I think we should focus on what Adam would like, and if he'd appreciate something more low-key, like just hanging out and celebrating together, then that's what we should do. Champagne still sounds good to me, though.
turns.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand that we're different, and that's okay. But for me, making my parents proud will always be important. As for Adam's celebration, I think we should get him something that shows we put thought into it, not just something like champagne that anyone can buy. How about we get him a book by his favorite author or something related to his field of study?
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I'm curious - Omar, when you mentioned your parents' perspective on gifts, and Kelly, when you talked about celebration traditions, it sounds like you both have really interesting family backgrounds that might shape how you think about marking special moments. Would you be willing to share a bit more about what those traditions mean to each of you?

turns.message: I'm curious - Omar, when you mentioned your parents' perspective on gifts, and Kelly, when you talked about celebration traditions, it sounds like you both have really interesting family backgrounds that might shape how you think about marking special moments. Would you be willing to share a bit more about what those traditions mean to each of you?

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I appreciate the interest, but for me, traditions around celebrations are deeply tied to family values. In my family, giving gifts that have personal meaning shows love and respect. I think it's important to acknowledge the journey that led to accomplishments, not just the celebration itself. That's why I lean towards something thoughtful for Adam. For us, it's not just about the moment, but the memories and significance behind it.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I get that, but I still think we should focus on celebrating Adam's achievement right now. The champagne idea really captures that joyful moment. And honestly, making my parents proud has never been a driving force for me. I believe in doing what feels right for me, not just what others expect. So, how about we just go with the champagne?
turns.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand that your perspective is different, and celebrating the moment is important too. However, making my parents proud is a fundamental value for me. I think we can celebrate Adam's achievement in a way that also honors our friendship and the journey we've shared. A personal gift can show him how much we care beyond just the celebration. What if we find a way to incorporate both ideas?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I see where you're coming from, but I still think the champagne is the way to go for a celebration like this. And about the whole making parents proud thing, I just don’t relate to that. My life choices are mine to make, and I want to focus on the here and now. Let's celebrate Adam with the champagne and enjoy the moment!
turns.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I respect your view on living in the moment, but I can't shake my belief in honoring my parents' sacrifices through my actions. Celebrating Adam is important, but I feel we can do that while also valuing the deeper connections we've had. It's not just about the now; it's about the memories we create and the significance behind our choices. I still think a thoughtful gift would be more meaningful for him.
